stories.headline: Congress politics of accusation and deceit .... Attempt to malign the Election Commission
stories.title: Congress politics of accusation and deceit .... Attempt to malign the Election Commission
stories.summary: Congress has called the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls a plot to that the party's own 1993 record with Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan weakens its claim to defend the Commission's independence. Rahul Gandhi and his party have found a new villain to prove that they are still relevant as opposition. It is the Election Commission of India. They say the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls is a plot. They call it "vote chori". They say it robs citizens of their vote. Some of them even want the Chief Election Commissioner to resign. It is a loud campaign. It is also a short-sighted one. Congress is the last party that should lecture anyone on the independence of the Election Commission. Its own record tells a different story. The man who scared them Go back to 1990. T. N. Seshan became Chief Election Commissioner. He did what few before him had dared. He enforced the Model Code of Conduct without fear. He cracked down on booth capturing. He stopped ministers from using government machinery to win votes. He made photo identity cards a reality. Politicians hated him. Every party felt the heat. But it was the Congress government at the Centre that acted. In 1993, the government of P. V. Narasimha Rao changed the structure of the commission. It had always been led by one man. Now it would have three members. The two new commissioners had equal powers. Decisions would be taken by majority. Look at the timing. Seshan was at the peak of his influence. The government was tired of being told no. Seshan saw the move for what it was. He went to the Supreme Court. The court upheld the new structure in 1995. The three-member commission stands to this day. Congress may call this reform. Most people who watched at the time called it an attempt to clip the wings of a strong umpire. The party that now cries foul Now compare that with today. Congress leaders speak as if they have always been guardians of the commission. They call it a puppet. They compare their struggle to the fight for freedom. They demand resignations. Where was this love for institutions in 1993? When an independent chief election commissioner became inconvenient, Congress cut him down to size. When the commission does a routine job today, Congress screams conspiracy. That is the definition of double standards. What SIR really is Let us be clear about what this exercise is. The revision of electoral rolls is not new. The law requires it. Its purpose is simple. Remove the names of the dead. Remove duplicate entries. Remove people who have moved elsewhere. Add new voters who are eligible. India is a vast country. People migrate for work. They marry and change homes. They die, and their names stay on the list for years. Any honest clean-up will remove many names. That is not a scandal. That is the job. The commission has said again and again that a wrongly deleted voter can apply to be added back. Booth Level Officers are available in every area. Online portals are open. Citizens can check their entries and correct them. So ask the Congress a plain question. If your voters are being deleted, where are the names? Where are the cases? Show them to the commission. Show them to the courts. A slogan is not evidence. What about those bogus voters, the Guspethias who were crying on the top of their voices, standing at the India-Bangladesh border, crying that we want to go back & we have voted in India several times but now we have to go back as the things have changed & more than 180 km of open borders will be sealed soon. Everyone saw those long queues of Guspethias patronised by TMC & Congress waiting to go back... The question they cannot answer Here is the biggest hole in their argument. They say names are being deleted to help the BJP. But how would the commission know who votes for whom? The voter list has no column for party choice. There is no tag that says "Congress voter". The ballot is secret. That is the whole point of it. To delete opponents on purpose, someone would have to know who they are. Congress has never explained this. It cannot. The theory falls apart the moment you think about it for a minute. Voters are not fooled The public is not buying it. Talk to ordinary people, and you hear the same thing. They want clean rolls. Fewer fake names mean a fairer contest. That helps every honest party. Many voters have already fixed their own entries. They went to the Booth Level Officer or used the online portal. They found it slow at times, but it worked. They do not feel like victims of a plot & are not buying Congress's baseless allegations. Assam is a good example. The state saw the same claims from Congress. Once the Election Commission explained the process, the allegations lost their force. Union Minister Pabitra Margherita made the point well when he said Assam had rejected Congress on SIR. Baseless attacks on institutions, he said, had become part of a political culture. People are tired of it. Every time Congress loses, it finds a new reason. First it was the voting machines. Now it is the voter list. Never once does it ask what went wrong in its own campaign, its own organisation or its own message. The cry that lost its meaning "Democracy is in danger," Congress says it before every election and after every defeat. Each time, the words mean a little less. Democracy was in real danger when the Emergency was imposed in 1975. Newspapers were censored. Opposition leaders were jailed. Courts were pressured. That was done by a Congress government. The party has no right to use the language of democratic crisis whenever it wants a headline. A mature opposition would do the hard work. It would send its workers door to door. It would find real errors and file real complaints. It would go to court with names and numbers. That is how a serious party behaves. Shouting "vote chori" from a stage is not the same as proving it. What the BJP believes Those are reasonable demands. The BJP has no problem with them. We want every eligible Indian to vote. We also want every fake name gone. No Guspethias to do bogus voting. What we reject is the idea that any clean-up of the rolls is an attack on democracy. It is the opposite. A dirty voter list is what weakens democracy. A clean one protects it. On appointments, the law of 2023 set up a selection panel that includes the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union minister. The Leader of the Opposition has a seat and a voice at the table. That is a long way from the old practice, under which the government of the day simply picked the chief. Congress used that old practice for decades and never once complained. Consistency is the test Institutions do not survive because they are free from criticism. They survive because they are judged by one standard, no matter who is in power. Congress fails that test. It cut down a strong commissioner when it held the Centre. Now it attacks the commission because it lost elections. It praises the umpire when it wins and abuses him when it loses. If Congress truly cares about the Election Commission, it should start with honesty. Admit what happened in 1993. Bring evidence, not slogans. Fight elections with ideas and work on the ground. Until then, its outrage will sound exactly like what it is. It is a party looking for someone to blame. (The author is a spokesperson for the BJP. stories.headline: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.title: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.summary: Mumbai: Aggregate revenue and net profit of the Nifty 50 companies are expected to grow in double digits year-on-year for the September quarter led by select companies from the automobiles, banking and finance, metals and oil and gas sectors. Revenue and net profit are likely to grow by 19.9% and 22.3% respectively according to the ETIG estimates. Their performance will also benefit from the lower base of 9% and 8.4% growth in revenue and profit in the year-ago quarter."The broader earnings outlook remains healthy, supported by improving domestic demand, strong credit growth, government spending and a recovery in private capex," said Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth.134753222Gautam Duggad, MD and Head of Sales, Institutional Equities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects Nifty earnings to grow by 27% and that of the companies covered by the broking firm to increase by 22%."Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings for the MOFSL Universe are expected to grow 24% year-on-year during the quarter," Duggad said.Read more: How a 9-year-old Warren Buffett learnt a lesson on compounding by rolling snowballs on the lawn of his Nebraska homeThe operating margin at the aggregate level is likely to contract by a tad 20 basis points to 21.9% from the year ago amid input cost inflation. Azzez expects margins to remain mixed as benefits of lower commodity costs are normalising while wage inflation and higher crude prices are creating some pressure on margins. "For capital goods, infrastructure and manufacturing, margins likely to remain stable to improving, supported by healthy order books, capacity utilisation and operating leverage," he mentioned, adding that for banking and finance companies, earnings growth would be driven more by strong loan growth than by expansion in margins.Read more: Why junk bonds deliver equity-like returns but with far inferior volatility, explains Saurabh MukherjeaDespite near-term challenges in the form of volatile energy prices, geopolitical and tariff risks, and weakening rupee against major currnecies, analysts are optimistic about medium-to-long term growth trajectory. Duggad believes that the risk-reward for Indian equities over a medium and long term has meaningfully improved given healthy earnings growth, resilient macroeconomic environment and cooling valuations. "With earnings growth increasingly concentrated in select themes, we expect market performance to remain firmly bottom-up, favouring growth-oriented businesses that are successfully scaling up and strengthening their competitive positioning," Duggad said. He expects 15-16% earnings growth over FY26-28 for the companies under his coverage.Azeez of Anand Rathi remains constructive for FY27 driven by strong healthy domestic demand and credit growth, government and private capital expenditure, and improving corporate earnings. "For FY27, Nifty 50 earnings per share (EPS) is expected to rise to ₹1,240 from ₹1,088 with 14% earnings growth," he said.Sector viewAutomobilesDemand across automobile segments remained resilient with sales volume growing in double digits year-on-year in the September quarter, barring lower tractor volume amid irregular monsoon. While revenue of majority of the auto makers is expected to rise in double digits, profits and profitability may remain muted due to higher input costs.BankingNet interest income is expected to grow in low double digits year-on-year while non-interest income may decline amid lower treasury income due to firm bond yields. Net interest margin may show weakness depending upon the extent of FCNR deposits raised by banks. The asset quality is likely to stay stable.Capital GoodsFresh orders from segments including power generation, transmission and distribution, data centres, and infrastructure kept the order book ringing during the quarter. While domestic execution gained pace amid scattered monsoon trend, geopolitical disturbance in the West Asian region may result in slower order ramp up. Higher raw material costs will weigh on profitability though the impact may soften due to pass-though of higher costs in some projects.CementCement demand is expected to grow in higher single digit in the September quarter, helped by sustained construction activities in an otherwise seasonally weak quarter due to monsoon. Demand was steady in the North, Western and Central regions. Cement prices showed a gradual recovery, largely to offset higher input costs. However, profitability is likely to remain under pressure.FMCGBarring ITC, fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are likely to report double digit revenue growth amid stable sales volume, higher product prices and low base in the year ago quarter. ITC is expected to show weaker sales volume, which is expected to result in lower revenue and profit for the quarter.Information TechnologyClients continued to observe caution while ramping up large, discretionary assignments. This is expected to keep top line growth muted for most top tier IT companies. The sequential revenue growth for the top tier companies is expected to remain under 2-3% for the quarte keeping currency rates constant. Operating margins may show a slight uptick in the absence of major wage increases for most of the top companies. Over 8.7% depreciation in the average rupee rate against the dollar during the quarter will support the rupee-denominated performanceMetalsElevated prices of aluminium, copper, and zinc are expected to help non-ferrous companies to post strong performance in the September quarter. Ferrous companies, too, are expected to benefit from firm domestic demand from the infrastructure segment.PharmaceuticalsCompanies with domestic focus are expected to show continued traction in the September quarter while US focused pharma companies such as Dr Reddy's Labs and Cipla are likely to report weakness with a double-digit drop in revenue. A weaker rupee is expected to soften the blow in reported profits.

stories.headline: India among 7 bidders to host 2036 Olympics
stories.title: India among 7 bidders to host 2036 Olympics
stories.summary: New Delhi’s bid plan centres around Ahmedabad city
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Lausanne: The ambitions of India to host the 2036 Olympics were confirmed on Tuesday by the IOC among seven bidders in the race.
India and Qatar have long been seen as favoured candidates in a hosting contest the IOC aims to decide in 2029 by a contested vote of its 100-plus members.
The members include Nita Ambani from India's richest family, and the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.
The International Olympic Committee said South Africa, South Korea, Germany, Hungary and Turkey also are in talks about a future hosting option with the 2040 edition and even 2044 also in view.
“But wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: Athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do,” said IOC President Kirsty Coventry, a two-time swimming gold medallist.
The IOC set an October 31 deadline for other national Olympic bodies to join the 2036 contest.
It also published a 30-page document on Tuesday to guide bidders.

India’s bid plan centers on the city of Ahmedabad, which will host the multi-sport Commonwealth Games in 2030 and has the world’s largest cricket stadium which is named after Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Qatar has hosted world championships in most top-tier Olympic sports, including soccer’s 2022 World Cup.
Its bid could yet expand from Doha to send some events to Gulf neighbours.
A Qatar-hosted Olympics should require the Summer Games to move from the July-August slot it has occupied at each edition from 2004 in Athens through 2032 in Brisbane.
A South Korean bid would be anchored in Seoul, which hosted the 1988 Summer Games, and spread across the country.
